A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TORA study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original assembly experiments, teacher probes, ablations, convergence measurements and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds loss-combination experiments, teacher-strength comparisons and three-seed statistical evaluations.

M1.justification: The RPF backbone, frozen teacher, projector, alignment objectives, token subsampling and inference procedure are unchanged. v2 clarifies CKA's status as the primary objective, already the default in v1; combined objectives are tested as ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions use Breaking Bad Everyday and Artifact, PartNet-Assembly, TwoByTwo, FRACTURA and Fantastic Breaks. The additional analyses use retained datasets and assembly scenarios; newly cited teacher-pretraining datasets were already documented in v1.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 introduces three comparison variants: CKA plus cosine, CKA plus NT-Xent, and all three losses together. Existing benchmark comparator sets, including Jigsaw, PMTR, CMNet, GARF and RPF in their corresponding experiments, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs test combined-loss configurations on TwoByTwo and compare cosine versus CKA using teachers grouped by strong or weak performance. Existing benchmark metrics, training budgets and anchor protocols are retained. The new statement about training across all categories is a disclosure, not evidence of a changed setting.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of CKA's contribution beyond teacher quality: Table 2 tests loss complementarity, Appendix D.5 compares strong and weak teachers, and D.4 controls teacher correlations for parameter count. Appendix G.2 additionally examines category shift versus inter-object assembly as explanations for NT-Xent failure, using existing benchmark results.

E5.justification: Appendix D.4 adds Fisher-transformed 95% confidence intervals, partial correlations and significance reporting for teacher probes. Appendix G.1 explicitly reports three-seed reruns, means and standard deviations, and paired t-tests for cosine versus CKA. This introduces substantial statistical validation absent from v1's documentation; the earlier run count is unspecified.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, zero-shot, efficiency and anchor-evaluation scores are unchanged. New supporting results include TwoByTwo PA of 71.5 for CKA versus 70.0, 68.5 and 67.7 for combined losses, teacher-specific CKA gains in Table A3, and three-seed aggregates in Table A5. These supplement rather than replace the original results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(18), mathematical definitions and stated CKA invariances are retained. The clarification that 'topological' means inter-token similarity structure adds terminology guidance, not a new formal definition, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: relational teacher alignment, geometry/contact-based teacher selection, late-layer alignment, faster convergence, improved assembly and zero inference overhead. New supporting analyses do not change these claims' scope.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the distribution-shift explanation for NT-Xent's TwoByTwo failure with an inter-object negative-pair mechanism. It also attributes combined-loss degradation to competing gradients, argues that CKA helps across teacher strengths, and acknowledges uncertainty from only six teachers. The original symmetry, contact-gap and teacher-capacity limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly states that models are trained across all object categories within each benchmark. Existing architecture details, hardware, optimization schedule, feature interpolation and project-page access remain unchanged; this is a limited clarification of the documented setup.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to C3G, PROSE, Geometric Action Model, Objaverse, ShapeNet, 3D-FUTURE and ABO. These extend background attribution without substantially changing the assembly/distillation positioning. Bibliographic updates to retained works are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 expands the explanation distinguishing token-wise baselines from CKA, clarifies 'topological,' adds analysis subsections and an Experimental Validation appendix section, and updates subsequent appendix labels. It also adds acknowledgements and corresponding-author notation, with localized language corrections; most existing prose and organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables: main Table 2 and appendix Tables A2, A3, A5 and A6. Existing tables and figures are relocated or resized and tables renumbered, while existing graphical content and qualitative examples are retained. The overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: The new ablations, teacher controls and uncertainty estimates make the unchanged method better supported and easier to assess. These benefits are tempered by overinterpretation: Appendix G.1 claims every comparison has p < 0.05 although Table A5 reports p = 0.64 for Breaking Bad PA, and G.2 infers a causal failure mechanism from comparisons containing only one inter-object benchmark. The added evidence provides a modest net improvement despite these localized weaknesses.
